notes: The warm climate ripens grapes easily, and winemakers more often need to add acid than sugar.
Chenin Blanc is often made to drink young, with rich tropical notes such as banana, guava, pear and pineapple.
Pinotage ranges from easy-drinking wine and rosé to barrel-aged reds for cellaring, and newer styles are brighter and juicier.
Stellenbosch Cabernet is known as heavy and full bodied, while Constantia's is herbal and minty.
The best Semillon is juicy, with a citrus perfume, fine texture and herbal notes.
Constantia was famous for an unfortified sweet wine made mostly from Muscat, and its estates still make sweet wines in homage, such as Vin de Constance.
Its Cabernet Sauvignon is known for herbal and minty flavors.
Stellenbosch Cabernet Sauvignon is noted for heavy, full bodied wines.
Western Cape wines range from sturdy Rhône-style reds to aromatic Sauvignon Blanc from vineyards cooled by Atlantic breezes.
Elgin is a high-lying, cool district in the Hottentots Holland mountains.
Its later-ripening, cooler sites give wines with exceptional fruit and elegance.
Chardonnay, Riesling, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir and Shiraz do particularly well.
Walker Bay is known for Chardonnay and Pinot Noir from the Hemel-en-Aarde wards.
Persistent cool winds from the nearby ocean give the area its cool climate.
Its Pinotage is noted for consistent quality, and fine Sauvignon Blanc, Merlot and Shiraz are made too.
Strong, cooling summer winds near Cape Agulhas give Elim a very cool ripening season.
That suits Sauvignon Blanc, and Semillon and Shiraz also show promise.
Cooling sea breezes, night mists and deep soils help Durbanville's grapes.
Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon draw the most attention.
Paarl's valley floor is hot before harvest, while vines on the eastern slopes hold water better.
Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinotage, Shiraz, Chardonnay and Chenin Blanc show the best potential.
Robertson's lime-rich soils and cooling southeasterly winds offset its hot summers.
Long seen as white wine country, it is known for Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc.
It also makes fine Shiraz and Cabernet Sauvignon, and the fortified dessert wines it was first famed for.
The Swartland was traditionally a source of robust, full-bodied reds and high-quality fortified wines.
Exciting reds and whites have emerged more recently, and it still makes top port-style wines.
Bush vines were the tradition, though trellising is spreading.
